g.text: Persist progress; make execution authority temporary
Arize separates durable issue history and skills from disposable sandboxes and bounded credentials.

Retain the request, inputs, permissions, tools, result, evaluator and relevant versions. Distinguish a run summary from the ordered trajectory. Trace agents modifying the system as well as deployed agents, so a proposed repair has evidence rather than only a confident explanation.

Issue history, useful skills and telemetry can survive a sandbox failure; temporary credentials and repository access should not survive by default. A replacement run resumes from durable state under newly checked authority. Persistence of knowledge does not imply persistence of permission.

Calibrate evaluators against human-labeled cases, replay a failure and inspect paired regressions. Proposed fixes or PRs remain proposals until accountable review permits release. Prime Intellect’s learning progression makes corrections an asset before pursuing routing or training optimizations.
Sources: Arize · Prime Intellect | Reviewed October 25, 2026
